main_text.p: bus urbium ad aggeres faciendos coguntur, quantus illorum numerus, & quam misere pereunt & trucidantur, principes id parum curant. At Deus in cuius conspectu præciosa est mors piorum, eorum curam gerit. Psal. 115. In bellis, vites, sepes arbores fructiferæ exuruntur, armenta & greges mactantur, & abiguntur, aut inopia pabuli pereunt, quæ causa est ut terra commode coli non posset.
Etiam pace facta, magnam & diuturnam caritatem, inopiam jumentorum, olei, lactis, butyri, caseï, carnis, lanæ aliarumq; rerum consequi necesse est.

Peste grassante, homines & jumenta pereunt: agri, quia non purgantur, fordescunt vineæ incultæ relinquuntur. Ita fames, caritas pestem comitantur, hæc enim duo ferè cohærent. Ideo Græcus una tantum litera λιμὸς fames & λοιμὸς pestis, differunt.

Etsi vero agricolæ nullis laboribus parcant in colendis agris & vinetis, tamen sæpe culturæ & laboribus non respondent. Rara enim est messis & vindemia. Præterea hyems longa & aspera sementem, vites, ar-

page.notes: Reading of the first word "bus" is uncertain: the line begins with a fragment, kept as printed. "præciosa" is printed as such (the expected word is pretiosa); printing error left as is. "λιμὸς" and "λοιμὸς" are transcribed from the Greek as printed; accents are read with some doubt. "fordescunt" and "caseï" are as printed. The line ending "ar-" continues on the next page.
